text:
For a **hotel conversion in Mexico where preserving the property’s identity and owner control is the priority**, I would consider the following soft brands and collections.

### Best initial shortlist

| Brand/collection | Best fit | Flexibility assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **Trademark Collection by Wyndham** | Upper-midscale through upscale urban hotels and resorts | **Very high.** Designed to retain the hotel’s name, story and design, with flexible standards. Wyndham already has several Trademark properties in Mexico, including urban and all-inclusive hotels. ([wyndhamhotels.com](https://www.wyndhamhotels.com/trademark/locations?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Registry Collection Hotels — Wyndham** | Luxury and upper-upscale resorts, especially all-inclusive | **Very high at the luxury end.** Owners retain substantial individuality while joining Wyndham’s distribution platform. Registry already has a meaningful resort presence in Mexico. ([development.wyndhamhotels.com](https://development.wyndhamhotels.com/upscale-lifestyle-hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Handwritten Collection — Accor** | Boutique upscale hotels and smaller lifestyle resorts | **Very high.** Accor describes it as conversion-friendly, operationally flexible and cost-effective, with the option to retain the existing hotel name. It is already represented in Mexico. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/news-stories/collection-brands-handwritten-emblems-mgallery?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Tapestry Collection by Hilton** | Upscale boutique, secondary-city and lifestyle hotels | **High.** Generally the more accessible Hilton collection for conversions; explicitly structured to preserve local character. Mexico examples include Perla La Paz. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hiltons-curio-and-tapestry-collections-celebrate-200th-hotel-milestones?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Curio Collection by Hilton** | Upper-upscale, distinctive resorts and larger urban hotels | **High, but with a higher quality threshold.** Strong choice when the owner wants individuality plus Hilton Honors and Hilton’s commercial platform. Hilton is using Curio for current Mexican conversions, including an announced Cancún all-inclusive resort. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hiltons-curio-and-tapestry-collections-celebrate-200th-hotel-milestones?utm_source=openai)) |
| **The Unbound Collection by Hyatt** | Upper-upscale and luxury boutique hotels with a strong story | **High.** Hyatt expressly positions it around independence, individuality and owner flexibility. The collection already operates in Mexico, including NUMU in San Miguel de Allende. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands/theunboundcollectionbyhyatt?utm_source=openai)) |

### Also worth testing

- **Tribute Portfolio — Marriott:** Probably Marriott’s most natural collection candidate for an upscale, design-led conversion.
- **Autograph Collection — Marriott:** Better for upper-upscale properties with a sufficiently distinctive concept and experience.
- **The Luxury Collection — Marriott:** Appropriate only for true luxury assets with substantial service, design and capital capacity. Marriott positions all three as operating models for independent hotels, backed by Marriott Bonvoy. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/premium-brands?utm_source=openai))
- **MGallery — Accor:** Strong for upper-upscale, story-driven boutique hotels and resorts. Accor already has an MGallery resort in Punta de Mita and emphasizes identity preservation in its conversion approach. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/hotel-development?li_ed=CwEAAAGXNpd3lV-YfM9wbzb_I0s3FE3yHpcRINj_uFPRmhTQfZxXlDd1thjx4ehqWhqqoTc4rB2APdrpVEkr-U9Zik_JUJqTdNx-KikeAOqplsKY9ZAf50G-AM21PQ&utm_source=openai))
- **Vignette Collection — IHG:** Attractive for a high-quality luxury or lifestyle conversion. IHG says properties can retain their name, look, feel and service identity while gaining access to IHG systems and loyalty. Its current Mexican footprint appears less established than those of Hilton, Wyndham or Marriott, so commercial contribution should be tested carefully. ([development.ihg.com](https://development.ihg.com/hotel-brands/vignette-collection?utm_source=openai))
- **WorldHotels Crafted, Elite or Distinctive — BWH Hotels:** Worth considering when maintaining independence is more important than obtaining the strongest consumer-facing brand name. WorldHotels is specifically organized around independent luxury and lifestyle hotels and already has properties in Mexico. ([development.bwhhotels.com](https://development.bwhhotels.com/content/luxury-hotels/en_US/hotel-development/development-collections.html?utm_source=openai))
- **BW Signature Collection or BW Premier Collection:** Potentially suitable for midscale-to-upscale conversions where a lighter affiliation and lower repositioning burden are priorities. ([development.bwhhotels.com](https://development.bwhhotels.com/content/developers/en_US/portfolio.html?utm_source=openai))

## Recommended priority by asset type

- **Urban upper-midscale/upscale:** Trademark, Tapestry, Handwritten, BW Signature/Premier.
- **Upper-upscale boutique or heritage hotel:** Curio, Autograph, Unbound, MGallery, WorldHotels Crafted/Elite.
- **Luxury resort:** Registry, Unbound, Vignette, Luxury Collection, Curio.
- **All-inclusive resort:** Registry or Trademark first; then Curio, Autograph or MGallery depending on positioning and operating model.

## Bottom line

If **maximum affiliation flexibility** is the overriding objective, I would begin with:

1. **Trademark Collection**
2. **Handwritten Collection**
3. **Registry Collection** for luxury or all-inclusive
4. **Tapestry Collection**
5. **WorldHotels/BW collections**

If the owner is willing to accept somewhat more brand oversight in exchange for a potentially stronger loyalty and distribution engine, add:

6. **Curio Collection**
7. **The Unbound Collection**
8. **Tribute Portfolio or Autograph Collection**

The final comparison should focus less on the “soft brand” label and more on the negotiated terms: **PIP cost, retention of the existing name, design waivers, mandatory systems and procurement, franchise versus management availability, F&B control, fee ramp-up, territorial protection and termination rights**. A soft brand can still become relatively prescriptive if those points are not negotiated carefully.
